requiredFindings.title: The synthetic Git reconstruction cannot silently replace the vcs:none law control
requiredFindings.problem: Item 20 explicitly requires the four T2 workspaces in vcs:none mode to give their overlay link maps, while item 19 and B-S1 require a conventional .git directory for actual membership. LD-B3B-6 recognizes the conflict but resolves it by adding synthetic conventional Git evidence and treating that different input as the specified control. That is a useful integration fixture, but it does not demonstrate the control on the stated vcs:none assembly. The plan also expressly leaves the optional git-conventional assembly successor S8 to B3-c.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Resolve the control interpretation at the law level before using this fixture as its discharge: obtain an accepted clarification/amendment of the item-20 control naming the synthetic reconstruction and its limits, or specify a separate declaration/link-only vcs:none control with supplied member evidence plus a distinct conventional-Git integration control. Do not claim that unchanged vcs:none product discovery admitted members, or that S8 has been implemented. Preserve exact pinned carrier/provider bytes and overlay-map comparison.

requiredFindings.title: Define the census equality projection and validate the new member cost paths
requiredFindings.problem: The plan requires byte-identical census records after re-pinning a changed closure, but the census record itself carries the closure pins, so the complete record cannot remain byte-identical. It also says every non-workspace project’s charges remain unchanged even though new declaration-reader work can occur with zero admitted members. No-member equality alone cannot establish an upper bound for the new member-aware traversal. Section 3’s record-equality tests do not test ledger usage against the extended cost model.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Name the exact unchanged comparison, such as repository-entry walker cost/population rows with an explicit allowlist for changed closure/reference metadata, rather than whole-record byte identity. Separate unchanged walker costs from added reader/member costs, including reader work at n=0. Require the revised native walk/member producer’s measured objects, edges and bytes to be bounded by the new model/bound on synthetic member, shared-path, exact-root, excluded/nested-member and boundary cases, including worst read growth/retries and root length. Retain the existing actual-versus-predicted cost checks and appropriate under-count mutations before using new workspace margins to close the gate.

requiredFindings.title: Keep the owner-required pre-run and post-run reviews as separate gates
requiredFindings.problem: LD-B3B-5 calls for rerunning the previously reviewed mode with a new closure, but B3-b3 groups the changed cost model/tool, blind refresh and resulting evidence into one reviewable step. The owner’s authorization explicitly requires review before and after the run. The original mode’s acceptance does not review newly changed cost/population/reference logic or its renewed receipt bindings. The plan does not identify a pre-run acceptance gate before opening held-out stores.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Within B3-b3, explicitly gate the mechanical run on acceptance of the exact updated tool, transitive cost/reference closure, receipt handling and synthetic confidentiality/lifecycle controls. Only then run the blind mode, followed by an independent review of the receipt and composed census. Preserve the closed output allowlist and no-inspection boundary. A fresh owner decision is not needed for this same authorized method and population; changing access or disclosure beyond that method would require separate authorization.

Its reference binding for tools/contracts/generator-closure.json is fe4bb4f4580706a556bb047c5a62ffc0a481b43dbc77984169a8fe8d2ea6fbd2, while the current file hashes to 796701ea87e7ff7db1b029c8c0eea043e550e9cd5f0daf234637fae927291acb (both 68,468 bytes).
